Pelvic organ prolapse with incomplete bl.description: Descent of the anterior vaginal wall and bladder (cystocele) can cause urinary stasis and high post-void residuals, predisposing to recurrent bacterial cystitis.

Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID).description: A primary immunodeficiency characterized by low immunoglobulin levels and impaired antibody responses that predispose to recurrent infections; while classically sinopulmonary, recurrent UTIs can occur.

Indolent lymphoproliferative disorder (e.normalized_text: Indolent lymphoproliferative disorder (e.g., chronic lymphocytic leukemia) considered and unlikely
Indolent lymphoproliferative disorder (e.description: CLL and other indolent lymphomas can cause hypogammaglobulinemia and recurrent bacterial infections with anemia, but typically show lymphocytosis, lymphadenopathy, or marrow involvement.

case: 95-year-old woman admitted after a fall. Medical history includes Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (on metformin). Laboratory findings showed elevated white cell count and C reactive protein levels. Urine culture revealed Klebsiella pneumoniae infection. Blood cultures were negative.

Acute complicated urinary tract infectio.normalized_text: Acute complicated urinary tract infection (UTI) due to Klebsiella pneumoniae
Acute complicated urinary tract infectio.description: Bacterial infection of the urinary tract in a high-risk host (elderly, diabetic), often presenting with systemic inflammatory response; Klebsiella species are common Gram-negative pathogens in older adults.

Acute pyelonephritis.description: Infection of the renal parenchyma typically due to ascending bacteria from the lower urinary tract, often causing systemic inflammation and bacteriuria.

Delirium superimposed on dementia (preci.normalized_text: Delirium superimposed on dementia (precipitated by infection)
Delirium superimposed on dementia (preci.description: Acute, fluctuating disturbance in attention and cognition occurring in a patient with baseline dementia, commonly triggered by infections such as UTIs in older adults and often leading to falls.

Urosepsis (sepsis secondary to urinary s.description: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection arising from the urinary tract; often associated with systemic inflammatory markers and may or may not have positive blood cultures.

Asymptomatic bacteriuria.description: Presence of bacteria in the urine without signs or symptoms of urinary tract infection; common in elderly women and those with diabetes.

case: 22-year-old athletic male presented with swelling and locking of the left knee. He had no recent trauma but had several football injuries as a child. Two years prior, he had experienced disabling knee pain.

Bucket-handle meniscal tear.description: A displaced longitudinal meniscal tear (often of the medial meniscus) that can cause mechanical locking and recurrent effusions, frequently related to prior sports injuries.

Osteochondritis dissecans with loose bod.description: Focal subchondral bone injury (often on the femoral condyle) that can lead to unstable cartilage and intra-articular loose bodies, causing mechanical symptoms and swelling in adolescents and young adults.

Synovial plica syndrome.description: Irritation or thickening of an embryologic synovial fold that can cause anterior knee pain, snapping, and pseudo-locking, often in active individuals.

Synovial chondromatosis.description: Benign metaplastic proliferation of synovium producing multiple cartilaginous loose bodies, leading to chronic swelling, pain, and mechanical locking.

Pigmented villonodular synovitis (tenosy.normalized_text: Pigmented villonodular synovitis (tenosynovial giant cell tumor)
Pigmented villonodular synovitis (tenosy.description: Proliferative synovial process causing recurrent monoarticular swelling, stiffness, and sometimes mechanical symptoms due to villonodular tissue or hemosiderin-laden nodules.

Discoid lateral meniscus.description: A congenital variant of the lateral meniscus that is thicker and more prone to tearing, causing snapping, locking, and effusions in children and young adults.

case: 48-year-old male presented with 1-week history of jaundice, dark brown urine, pale stools, and nausea. Medical history and physical exam were unremarkable. Laboratory findings showed hepatic panel in cholestatic pattern: total bilirubin 117 μmol/L, conjugated bilirubin 66.8 μmol/L, alkaline phosphatase 173 IU/L, γ-Glutamyltransferase 380 IU/L, Alanine transaminase 468 IU/L. CA19-9 was 11783 IU/mL. Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and β2-microglobulin were normal.

diagnoses.name: Primary pancreatic T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma
diagnoses.normalized_text: Primary pancreatic T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma

Pancreatic head adenocarcinoma (obstruct.normalized_text: Pancreatic head adenocarcinoma (obstructing distal bile duct)
Pancreatic head adenocarcinoma (obstruct.description: Malignancy of the pancreatic head that commonly causes distal common bile duct obstruction, leading to painless obstructive jaundice and cholestatic liver enzyme abnormalities.

Extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (distal.description: A malignant tumor of the extrahepatic bile ducts that causes biliary obstruction and cholestasis; often associated with markedly elevated CA19-9.

Choledocholithiasis with obstructive jau.description: Gallstones within the common bile duct causing obstruction and cholestasis; may present acutely with jaundice and abnormal cholestatic liver tests.

Gallbladder carcinoma with biliary obstr.description: Malignancy arising from the gallbladder that can invade or compress the biliary tree, leading to obstructive jaundice and elevated cholestatic enzymes; CA19-9 can be elevated.

Primary sclerosing cholangitis with domi.normalized_text: Primary sclerosing cholangitis with dominant stricture
Primary sclerosing cholangitis with domi.description: A chronic, immune-mediated cholangiopathy causing multifocal biliary strictures and cholestasis; dominant strictures can acutely obstruct bile flow and raise CA19-9.

Drug-induced cholestasis (e.g., from ant.normalized_text: Drug-induced cholestasis (e.g., from antibiotics or anabolic steroids)
Drug-induced cholestasis (e.g., from ant.description: Medication-related impairment of bile formation or flow leading to conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and cholestatic enzyme elevation.

case: 80-year-old woman with 6-month history of slowly increasing asymptomatic lumbar subcutaneous mass. History of chronic renal failure requiring dialysis three times weekly for 10 years. Poor compliance with phosphate-binding medications and dietary restrictions. Physical exam showed firm, immobile subcutaneous nodule measuring 9 cm in major axis. Laboratory findings: serum calcium 1.95 mmol/L (normal: 2.05-2.55), serum phosphorus 3.3 mmol/L (normal: 0.74-1.52), serum intact parathyroid hormone 142 ng/L (normal: 10-65), serum creatinine 787 μmol/L (normal: 53-106).

Uremic tumoral calcinosis (metastatic so.description: Deposition of calcium-phosphate salts in periarticular or subcutaneous soft tissues, typically in patients with end-stage renal disease and hyperphosphatemia, often associated with secondary hyperparathyroidism.

Metastatic calcinosis cutis due to secon.normalized_text: Metastatic calcinosis cutis due to secondary hyperparathyroidism
Metastatic calcinosis cutis due to secon.description: Widespread or localized calcium salt deposition in skin/subcutis from high calcium-phosphate product, commonly seen in chronic kidney disease with secondary hyperparathyroidism.

Calciphylaxis (calcific uremic arteriolo.description: Medial calcification of small arterioles leading to ischemia and painful necrotic skin lesions in patients with ESRD, often associated with high phosphate and secondary hyperparathyroidism.

Soft tissue sarcoma.description: Malignant tumor of mesenchymal origin presenting as a deep, firm, enlarging soft tissue mass, often painless and larger than 5 cm.

Tophaceous gout.description: Chronic deposition of monosodium urate crystals forming firm subcutaneous tophi, typically in patients with longstanding hyperuricemia and gout.

case: 47-year-old female presented to emergency department after being hit while skiing by another skier at high speed from behind. Immediate pain and marked general swelling of the knee joint occurred after impact. Unable to bear weight. Physical exam showed neurovascularly intact limb with no broken skin. No relevant medical, family, or social history.

Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear.description: Acute ligament injury often caused by pivoting or valgus stress that leads to knee instability and hemarthrosis.

Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) tear.description: Injury to the PCL typically from a posteriorly directed force on the proximal tibia (e.g., dashboard injury or collision from behind), causing acute pain and swelling.

Tibial plateau fracture.description: Fracture of the proximal tibial articular surface often due to high-energy trauma, associated with acute pain, joint effusion, and inability to bear weight.

Meniscal tear.description: Tear of the knee’s fibrocartilaginous meniscus, typically from twisting injuries, leading to pain and impaired weight-bearing; swelling often develops over hours.

Patellar dislocation (spontaneously redu.description: Transient lateral displacement of the patella, often in twisting or valgus mechanisms, causing acute pain, large effusion, and difficulty weight-bearing; it may reduce before evaluation.

Osteochondral fracture of the knee.description: Fracture involving articular cartilage and subchondral bone, often from high-energy impact or associated with ligamentous injury, causing hemarthrosis and acute pain.

case: A 52-year-old woman presented with complaints of anal pain, constipation, and tenesmus for 3 months before being referred to the hospital. There were no relevant prior illnesses. Rectal digital examination revealed a 6-cm smooth elastic mass on the rectal posterior left side 2 cm from the anal verge. Colonoscopy showed a rectal submucosal bulging. Computed tomography scan and magnetic resonance imaging confirmed the presence of a single 6-cm well-delimited mass, compressing and infiltrating the wall of the medium to low rectum.

diagnoses.name: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
diagnoses.icd11_title: Gastrointestinal stromal tumour of unspecified gastrointestinal sites

Rectal gastrointestinal stromal tumor (G.description: A mesenchymal tumor arising from interstitial cells of Cajal; rectal GISTs often present as submucosal, well-demarcated masses that can compress or invade the rectal wall and cause obstructive or pain symptoms.

Rectal leiomyosarcoma.description: A malignant smooth muscle tumor of the rectum that typically presents as a large submucosal mass; it can invade locally and cause pain, constipation, and tenesmus.

Rectal schwannoma.description: A benign nerve sheath tumor that can arise in the rectal wall; usually well-circumscribed and submucosal, causing compressive symptoms when large.

Rectal neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid),.description: A neuroendocrine tumor arising from enterochromaffin cells; rectal NETs are usually small and submucosal, but larger lesions (>2 cm) can invade deeper layers and cause obstructive symptoms.

Primary rectal lymphoma.description: An uncommon extranodal lymphoma involving the rectum, often presenting as a submucosal mass that may cause obstructive symptoms; can be well-circumscribed but may also infiltrate the wall.

case: Two-year-four-month-old female with IUGR at birth (39 weeks, cesarean delivery for placenta failure), birth weight 1850 g, length 44.5 cm, and head circumference 31 cm, all at the 3rd percentile. At 3 months, she was evaluated for suspected hearing loss; ABR showed bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss, and hearing aids were placed at 4 months. During infancy, she had poor weight and height gain below the 3rd percentile, with otherwise normal psychomotor development (sitting at 8 months, walking at 14 months, talking at 13 months). CNS MRI was normal. Genetic testing identified a de novo heterozygous PIK3R1 variant c.1956dupT (p.Lys653*) in exon 15.

SHORT syndrome (PIK3R1-related).description: A rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in PIK3R1, characterized by intrauterine growth restriction, postnatal short stature, partial lipodystrophy, insulin resistance/diabetes, distinctive facial features, ocular findings (Rieger anomaly), delayed dentition; sensorineural hearing loss can occur in some cases.

Activated PI3K-δ Syndrome 2 (APDS2, PIK3.description: An autosomal dominant primary immunodeficiency due to specific PIK3R1 variants (often splice-site) causing PI3Kδ pathway hyperactivation; features include recurrent sinopulmonary infections, lymphadenopathy/splenomegaly, autoimmunity, growth delay, and elevated transitional/naive B cells.

Congenital cytomegalovirus (CMV) infecti.description: A congenital infection that can cause IUGR, microcephaly, periventricular calcifications, hepatosplenomegaly, chorioretinitis, and congenital sensorineural hearing loss; neurodevelopmental impairment varies.

Waardenburg syndrome.description: An autosomal dominant disorder characterized by congenital sensorineural hearing loss and pigmentary abnormalities of the hair, skin, and eyes, sometimes with dystopia canthorum depending on subtype.

Pendred syndrome / DFNB4 with enlarged v.description: A recessive disorder featuring congenital or early-onset sensorineural hearing loss (often fluctuating/progressive) associated with enlarged vestibular aqueduct and/or Mondini malformation; thyroid enlargement (goiter) and variable thyroid dysfunction may appear later.
